deep.reconstruction:
This page is the draft of the core passage of §3 ('Stetigkeit der geraden Linie') of Dedekind's 'Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen' (1872; dated in the preface to Nov. 1858 for the discovery). It contains no computation. It contains one definitional or axiomatic principle and its motivation.

(1) Context from the previous page. The rationals Q, compared with the points of a line L, are 'gappy' (lückenhaft, unstetig), while L is held to be continuous (stetig). The question is what continuity consists in. Only the answer will give a scientific foundation for the study of all continuous domains.

(2) Recalled fact from the previous section (property of the ordered line). Every point a of L divides L into two pieces A1, A2 such that every point of A1 lies left of (<) every point of A2. Dedekind leaves aside here which piece takes a itself; in the print a may be assigned to either.

(3) The 'Fund', i.e. the converse, taken as the essence of continuity. Suppose L = A1 ∪ A2 with A1, A2 nonempty and disjoint, and with x < y for all x in A1 and all y in A2. Then there exists one and only one point a that produces this division. That is, for all x in A1 and y in A2: x ≤ a ≤ y, so a = max A1 or a = min A2.

In modern terms: every Dedekind cut of the linearly ordered set L is produced by a unique element. This is order-completeness, equivalent for a dense order to the least-upper-bound property.
- Uniqueness is automatic in a dense order (my remark). If a < b both produced the cut, a point c with a < c < b would have to lie in A1 and in A2.
- Existence is the substantive content.

(4) Dedekind expects everyone to grant the truth of the statement at once ('sofort'). He also expects most readers to be disappointed that this triviality reveals the 'secret of continuity'. The next page continues: it is an unprovable axiom by which we 'think continuity into' the line.

The implicit contrast, made explicit elsewhere in the 1872 text, is with Q. The cut A1 = {x in Q : x ≤ 0 or x^2 < 2}, A2 = {x in Q : x > 0, x^2 > 2} has no rational producing element, because x^2 = 2 has no rational solution.
errors: No mathematical errors. The draft formulation tacitly assumes both classes are nonempty, as does the printed version; the 'Eintheilung aller Punkte in zwei Klassen' implies it.

results.what: Continuity of the line characterized as: every partition of its points into two classes, with every point of the first left of every point of the second, is produced by exactly one point (converse of the fact that each point cuts the line).
results.usually_credited_to: Richard Dedekind, 'Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen' (1872); conceived Nov. 1858

results.what: Uniqueness of the producing point (stated as 'ein und nur ein Punkt').
results.modern_name: Uniqueness of cut element in a dense linear order

deep.surprise_reason: This is a manuscript draft of the famous, published §3 of 'Stetigkeit und irrationale Zahlen'. It is nearly verbatim the printed text, apart from small wording changes (e.g. 'Prinzip' inserted in the margin, 'Behauptung ... sofort'). The interest is purely textual-genetic.

checkable.asserts: The only roots are ±sqrt(2), which are irrational. So the cut of Q given by x**2 < 2 versus x**2 > 2 (x > 0) has no rational producing element: Q is not Dedekind-complete.
x**2 - 2 has no rational roots (rational root test).
Density: for a < b the midpoint lies strictly between them, which yields uniqueness of a cut-producing point.

transcription_corrections: Line 3: 'alles stetigen Gebiete' should read 'aller stetigen Gebiete' ('aller' is underlined in the MS).
Line 1: the struck word after 'man' is uncertain; 'ihr' is doubtful.
The marginal insertion reads ', also in folgendem Princip:' (spelled with c, as on the next page, 'Princips'). The duplicated colon in the transcription is an artifact of the insertion mark.
Near the bottom: the word written above 'Behauptung' is 'sofort', giving 'die Wahrheit dieser Behauptung sofort zugeben wird' (cf. the printed text). It is not a repeated 'Behauptung'.
The 'Z' of 'Zerfallen' is boxed or emphasized in the MS.
The struck phrase reads approximately 'Zerschneidung der Geraden in zwei' and is replaced by 'Eintheilung aller Punkte'; 'aller' is written above the struck 'der'.
The page carries the foliation/page number '7' at top right. A stray 'in' appears in the left margin near the 'Behauptung' line.
